title: Egypt’s royal tomb builders staged one of history’s first strikes
body: Around 1158 BC, in the 29th year of Ramesses III’s reign, the artisans of Deir el-Medina, who cut and decorated the royal tombs in the Valley of the Kings, put down their tools because their grain rations had not arrived. They staged sit-ins at temples and told officials, ‘We are hungry’. Grain was released, and the dispute was written down on a papyrus now kept in Turin.
